capabilities: Track a ward-round Today view of inpatients, overdue work, and upcoming tasks
Manage patient episodes, pathways, priorities, tasks, and discharge or archive flows
Log OR bookings and completed procedures in a surgery logbook with portfolio counts
Export filtered patient lists as Obsidian tables or CSV spreadsheets
Run clinical data integrity checks with Sync-aware read-only recovery
disambiguation: Not an EHR/EMR, prescribing, or clinical decision-support tool; the README describes it as a personal workflow aid with no encryption or compliance certification.
extras: Extensive security and privacy documentation warns against storing identifiable data without institutional approval; the desktop surgery-logbook CSV export is a separate Node.js command not bundled with the plugin; iPhone capture inbox requires a supported iOS/Obsidian version and physical widget testing is outstanding; requires Obsidian 1.13.0 or later.
problem: Obsidian has no structured, mobile-friendly system for managing personal patient follow-up, episode tasks, and surgical procedure logs as local records.

relations.evidence: install BRAT, run BRAT: Add a beta plugin for testing

summary: Mobile-first clinical workspace that tracks patients, care episodes, tasks, and surgery logbook entries as Markdown notes with YAML properties.
